findings.title: Unverified JWT token decode enables authentication bypass
findings.impact: Attacker can forge arbitrary JWT tokens with any claims (sub, role, tenant) by crafting a malicious token, bypassing all authentication checks. Impacts both currentUser() and tagRequest() functions which use jwt.decode() without verification.
findings.evidence: jwt.decode(bearer) at lines 6 and 12 processes untrusted JWT header without calling jwt.verify(). The jwt.decode() method parses but does not validate signature or expiration. No secret key is passed, allowing any token to be accepted.
findings.recommendation: Replace jwt.decode() with jwt.verify(bearer, SECRET_KEY) on both lines 6 and 12. Implement proper JWT secret management (env var or key store). Add error handling for invalid/expired tokens. Verify claims (sub, role, tenant) only after successful signature validation.

findings.title: SQL injection via unparameterized ORDER BY clause
findings.impact: Attacker can inject arbitrary SQL through the 'order' query parameter, potentially exfiltrating all data from the invoices table, modifying data, or executing database functions. Example: ?order=created_at;DROP TABLE invoices;--
findings.evidence: Line 24: db.query(`SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE owner_id = $1 ORDER BY ${order}`, [req.user.id]) concatenates req.query.order directly into the SQL string. Unlike the $1 parameter for owner_id, the ORDER BY clause is not parameterized. The /payments endpoint at line 32 uses a SORTABLE allowlist (correct pattern), but /invoices does not.
findings.recommendation: Use an allowlist of permitted ORDER BY columns (e.g., {created_at, updated_at, amount}). Validate req.query.order against the allowlist before building the query. Example: const column = ALLOWED_SORTS[req.query.order] || 'created_at'; then use the column variable in the query.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) on invoice detail endpoint
findings.impact: Attacker can view any invoice by ID without owner verification. Endpoint returns full invoice data if it exists, regardless of who owns it. User can enumerate and exfiltrate invoices belonging to other customers.
findings.evidence: Line 7-10: GET /invoices/:id queries 'SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE id = $1' but does not check if req.user.id matches the owner_id. Contrast with the /receipts/:id endpoint (line 13-18) which correctly includes 'AND owner_id = $2' check. The /invoices list (line 24) and /payments list (line 32) both check owner_id correctly, but the detail endpoint does not.
findings.recommendation: Add owner_id check to the query: change line 8 query to 'SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE id = $1 AND owner_id = $2', [req.params.id, req.user.id]. Verify that req.user.id is populated by authentication middleware (currently depends on unverified JWT from F-001).

findings.title: Cross-site scripting (XSS) in invoiceNote function via unescaped HTML
findings.impact: If invoiceNote() is called with attacker-controlled note text, the HTML template directly renders it without escaping, allowing injection of arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the user's browser. XSS can steal session tokens, modify invoice data, or redirect to phishing sites.
findings.evidence:
Line 4-6: invoiceNote() returns `
${note}
` with note interpolated directly into HTML. No escaping applied. Contrast with customerName() (line 9-11) which correctly uses escapeHtml(name). If req.body.note or user-submitted invoice notes reach this function, attacker can inject
findings.recommendation:
Wrap note with escapeHtml: return `
${escapeHtml(note)}
`;. Audit all callers of invoiceNote() to confirm that user input flows through it. Apply the same escaping to any other user-controlled fields rendered as HTML.

findings.title: Server-side request forgery (SSRF) in fetchLogo via open redirect and no URL allowlist
findings.impact: Attacker can use the /branding/preview endpoint to fetch internal resources (localhost services, cloud metadata endpoints like 169.254.169.254, or internal APIs). With redirect: 'follow', the attacker can also bypass redirects to exfiltrate credentials or leak sensitive data.
findings.evidence: Line 5-8: fetchLogo(url) calls fetch(url) with redirect: 'follow' on any URL. No domain allowlist (contrast with fetchAsset at line 11-16 which has ALLOWED set). Attacker request: POST /branding/preview {"logoUrl": "http://localhost:8080/admin"} or "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/" would be fetched directly.
findings.recommendation: Add URL validation and allowlist to fetchLogo: parse the URL, validate hostname against a whitelist (e.g., cdn.example.com, assets.example.com). Change redirect to 'error' to disable open redirects. Add timeout (5 seconds) and size limits (max 10MB) to prevent hanging or DoS. Example: const parsed = new URL(url); if (!ALLOWED.has(parsed.hostname)) throw new Error('host not allowed');
